name: bossa
desc: Flash utility for Atmel SAM microcontrollers
why: Flashes firmware onto Atmel SAM boards; a hands-on hardware tool, close call on interest.

brief.what_it_is: BOSSA is a flash programming utility for Atmel's SAM family of flash-based ARM microcontrollers. The README calls it a replacement for Atmel's SAM-BA software. The package installs two executables, bossac and bossash. The README does not show command syntax, inputs, or outputs, so beyond flashing firmware onto SAM boards, the details are not confirmed here.
brief.why_it_exists: The stated motivation is to create a simple, easy-to-use, open source utility to replace Atmel's SAM-BA software. BOSSA is an acronym for Basic Open Source SAM-BA Application, which reflects that goal.
brief.install_notes: The README gives no install steps beyond the brew package. Device support depends on hardware: the README lists supported SAM device families and notes that several are untested per release. Hardware donors include Atmel, David Crocker, and Adafruit, which suggests testing relies on physical development boards.
brief.standout: The project is a community-maintained replacement for a vendor tool, and its README is open about which device families are actually tested with each release versus which are listed but may break. It also solicits donated development boards to add test coverage.
brief.status: Version 1.9.1 is named in the README. No release date or last-commit date was visible on the page I fetched, so recency is not confirmed. The README does not mark the project as abandoned, and the contributor-driven device testing note suggests ongoing work. Overall status is unknown, leaning toward maintained based only on the version label.
brief.caveats: Several listed device families (SAM3X, SAM3A, SAM7L, SAM9XE, SAMR21, SAML21, SAME51, SAME53, SAME54, SAME70, SAMS70, SAMV70, SAMV71) are marked with an asterisk as not tested for each release and could stop working. The README gives no command examples, so usage is not documented on the homepage. The project is BSD licensed. Brew's caveats field was empty.
